newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps down, CFDs drop 10 cts, fuel falls.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps down, CFDs drop 10 cts, fuel falls.

text.p: European oil swaps fell decisively on Thursday after edging cautiously higher earlier this week.
Market confidence remains fragile and Brent CFDs in particular seem vulnerable to downward pressure.
Brent CFDs fell more than 10 cents a barrel, extending losses seen in the morning.
Next week traded at 64 and 66.50 cents under June while the following three weeks talked 57 cents, 48 cent and 42 cents under June respectively. Wet Brent was pegged just over $1 a barrel below June.
Gasoline lost $1 a tonne but fuel fell $3 a tonne. April
gasoline swaps slumped $2 a tonne after barge trade at $190 and possibly as low as $188 for prompt.
The more liquid May swaps were just $1 lower at $194.50 with June slipping to $192.50. Dealers said crack spreads were little changed.
Heavy fuel swaps lost $3 a tonne with May barges talking around $82 by late afternoon following trade at $80 for May on cargoes.
Low sulphur was quiet but notionally talking around $88 for April but nearer $86.50 for May.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent were little changed with the third quarter valued at $4.30 a barrel and the three subsequent quarters at $4.85, $4.65 and $4.05 respectively.
Jet premiums held around $24 a tonne above the IPE for April and $25 above for May. The third quarter was $27.50 above and the fourth $33 above.
